correctness.rationale: A disjoint-support escape argument gives the universal lower bound 2^(1/p) in every infinite-dimensional sigma-finite Lp. For p<=2 the appropriate Clarkson inequality gives the matching upper bound. For p>2 atomless, the probability measure |x|^p dmu can be split exactly in half, and y=(2 1_A-1)x makes both distances exactly 2^(1-1/p), matching Clarkson. If an atom A exists, the normalized indicator of A is a base vector; any y is scalar on A, and the smaller sign has pth-power distance (1-a)^p+1-a^p<=2, forcing 2^(1/p). The measure-theoretic and p=2 boundaries are correct.

final_claim: For complete sigma-finite measure spaces with infinite-dimensional real L_p(mu), s(L_p(mu))=2^(1/p) for p<=2; for p>2 it is 2^(1-1/p) in the atomless case and 2^(1/p) whenever an atom is present.
